description: Change ONE existing record. Link fields go in 'rels', subform fields in 'subforms'. The answer says each cell's change — `changed` (was → now) and `unchanged`. A row holds one value per field: a second call on the SAME record_id replaces what the first wrote, so several names mean several rows — a different record_id for each, and create_record for the ones no row is left for.

data.description: Plain fields to change: { key: value }; a key is the field's id, its name or its html_name (get_form_fields)

rels.description: Rel fields: { "rel field name": "record ID" } or { "rel field name": ["id1", "id2"] } for many-to-many

subforms.description: Subform fields: { "subform field_id": { "form_id": "subform ID", "records": [{"field_id": "value"}] } }. NOTE: 'records' is ALWAYS an array of hash objects [{field_id: value}]. NEVER write an array of numbers [1, 2] or plain IDs!

values.description: An alias of data — may be used in its place

name: update_record
